articles.title: Africa: Deadly Viruses Know No Borders, Nor Should Our Resolve to Stop Them
articles.summary: [allAfrica] In this guest column for AllAfrica, the Dutch Trade and Development Minister and the head of the World Health Organization stress that addressing viral health crises anywhere protects everyone everywhere. The government of the Netherlands is committing funding both for the current Ebola crisis and flexible funding to quickly respond to new or emerging global threats.
articles.hausa_translation: Afrika: Cutar da take kasua ba su da iyaka, haka kuma ya kamata a yi wa yunkuri na tsare su. A wannan labarin, Ministan Kasua da Haɓaka na Nederanda da shugaban Hukumar Lafiya ta Dunia suna bayyana cewa magance aukacin lafiya a waje ya kare kowa a duk waje. Gwamnatin Nederanda ta talata kudi don matsalar Ebola da kuma kuɗi na jiya don amsa sariƙa da sabon cutarwa.
critical_questions: Why is Netherlands framing this as their leadership issue when the primary burden falls on African health systems and communities?
What specific mechanisms ensure 'flexible funding' reaches frontline responders rather than international bureaucracies?
Are emerging viral threats being addressed equally or do wealthy nations prioritize threats near their borders?
What evidence shows previous international commitments to pandemic preparedness were actually implemented in African nations?
Whose voices are absent—which African health officials, local researchers, or affected communities are quoted in this piece?

The

Are private healthcare providers and informal medicine vendors included in this training, or does it only reach public facilities?
What independent verification exists for improved diagnostic accuracy post-training compared to baseline measurements?

articles.title: REA flags off 18.8MW mini-grid projects to connect 125,106 Zamfara households
articles.summary: By Udeme AkpanThe Rural Electrification Agency (REA) has flagged off the development of 37 mini-grid projects with a combined solar generation capacity of approximately 18.8 megawatts-peak (MWp) in Zamfara State. The projects, comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated mini-grids, are expected to connect 125,106 households across Gummi, Gusau, Kaura Namoda, Maradun, Shinkafi, Tsafe and Zurmi [&
articles.hausa_translation: Hukumar Sarrafa Waje ta Kasua (REA) ta fara aiki kan abubuwan sarrafa waje masu karfi 18.8MW a jihar Zamfara, wanda zai haɗa gidaje 125,106 a gari bakwai daban-daban.

articles.title: $2bn Afreximbank fund targets Africa’s creative economy as CANEX opens in Lagos
articles.summary: By Elizabeth Onyogha Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026 opened in Lagos yesterday, bringing together leading creatives, investors, policymakers, business leaders and cultural figures from across Africa and the diaspora to explore investment, financing and commercial opportunities in the continent’s creative economy. Hosted by the Federal Government of Nigeria and organised by the African Expo

Why is Creative Africa Nexus organized by 'African Expo' with minimal detail on governance structure, and who benefits most from this intermediary arrangement?
What evidence exists that previous large African development funds targeting creative sectors have achieved measurable economic returns for grassroots creators versus institutional players?

articles.title: Nigeria lost 3.3m barrels to oil thieves in 2025 – NUPRC

How does this 3.3m barrel figure compare to previous years, and is the trend improving or worsening?
Which international oil companies and their security contractors are involved in these supply chains, and what accountability exists?

articles.title: Sokoto: Tambuwal expresses worry over alleged political intolerance

articles.title: Ex-gov hails massive turnout at Atiku’s Sokoto campaign

articles.title: Tinubu to embark on two-day official visit to Akwa Ibom, Rivers

articles.title: Former Cross River PDP chair doubts party’s 2027 chances

articles.title: EFCC: We’re being harassed over Yahaya Bello’s case
